THEVENIN'S THEOREME
The purpose of Thevenin's theorem is to reduce a complex circuit to a simple circuit when repeated calculations of the load resistor are required. Enter the discussion text here.
DISCUSSION
For example, in this circuit voltage and current through the load can be calculated using Ohm's law. The process requires many calculations. This is an overlay page.
When using Ohm's Law, if the value of RL is changed, you will have to recalculate the entire circuit to determine the new voltage and current on the load.
Using Thevenin's Theorem the complex circuit is reduced to a single source and a single resistance. This is an overlay page.
Then any value of load can be placed across terminals A and B. Circuit values are easily calculated. This is an overlay page.
Thevenin's Theorem states that the entire network connected to A and B can be replaced by a single voltage source (Vth) and a single series resistance (Rth).
Thevenin's Theorem states that the entire network connected to A and B can be replaced by a single voltage source (Vth) and a single series resistance (Rth). Enter the discussion text here.
